8.0.0.en: 1 And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, wherein Solomon had built the house of the LORD, and his own house, 2 That the cities which Huram had restored to Solomon, Solomon built them, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there. 3 And Solomon went to Hamathzobah, and prevailed against it. 4 And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store cities, which he built in Hamath. 5 Also he built Bethhoron the upper, and Bethhoron the nether, fenced cities, with walls, gates, and bars; 6 And Baalath, and all the store cities that Solomon had, and all the chariot cities, and the cities of the horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and throughout all the land of his dominion.

8.0.1.en: Some see that Solomon was occupied with practical construction, and although he was a man of knowledge, understanding, learning and wisdom, it is not recorded of him that he devoted himself to study and meditation. Yet his doing of many works shows that in his private life he cared for the word of God and meditated on it. This appeared through the work of the Holy Spirit of God, who inspired him with the holy books, namely Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, the Song of Songs and Wisdom. Also his prayer in the temple reveals his study of the Law, especially the Book of Deuteronomy. All this suggests to us that he did not neglect his studies, his readings and his meditations.

8.0.2.en: And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, wherein Solomon had built the house of the LORD, and his own house [1]

8.0.3.en: That the cities which Huram had restored to Solomon, Solomon built them.

8.0.4.en: He cared for the church building, that is, the temple of the Lord and its annexes, as he cared for his palace and for building or renewing some cities, and for working for the comfort of his wife, the daughter of Pharaoh, outside the house of David, and for looking after the workers from among the Gentiles and the men of the Lord from among his own people, and for the ordering of worship and service.

8.0.5.en: Here we see Huram king of Tyre giving cities to Solomon, which points to God’s work with the Church of the New Testament, where the world hands over splendid cities to the Church of Christ, which receive the faith and are filled with peace.

8.0.6.en: He had already referred to these cities that the king of Tyre gave to Solomon (1 Kgs 9:11-13).

8.0.7.en: Here he did not mention the mistake that Solomon made in giving twenty cities of the land of Galilee to Hiram, which Hiram despised, calling them “the land of Cabul,” that is, trifling and worthless (1 Kgs 9:11-14). On the one hand, the king of Tyre despised these cities that were in the region of the Promised Land; on the other, there was unfaithfulness in this conduct, for Solomon disposed of the possession of the land of the Lord and handed it over to the Gentiles.

8.1.0.en: and caused the children of Israel to dwell there. [2]

8.2.0.en: And Solomon went to Hamathzobah, and prevailed against it. [3]

8.2.1.en: Hamathzobah: either the Hamath known today, or another Hamath in the kingdom of Zobah.

8.3.0.en: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store cities, which he built in Hamath. [4]

8.4.0.en: Also he built Bethhoron the upper, and Bethhoron the nether, fenced cities, with walls, gates, and bars; [5]

8.5.0.en: And Baalath, and all the store cities that Solomon had, and all the chariot cities, and the cities of the horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and throughout all the land of his dominion. [6]

8.5.1.en: The Lord allowed him to build not only what the state needed, but also all that Solomon desired, and so he was extravagant in expenses and constructions. This afterward drove him to the luxury that corrupted his life, especially as he married many wives, for one reason or another, and he burdened the people with the payment of taxes, which caused the division of the kingdom immediately after his death, when his son Rehoboam took the throne. For ten tribes joined Jeroboam, who broke away and formed the kingdom of the north.

8.5.2.en: This is recorded in the Book of Kings, but Chronicles focused on the bright side connected with worship, and left the weaknesses and falls to be recorded by the Book of Kings.

8.6.0.en: 7 As for all the people that were left of the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which were not of Israel, 8 But of their children, who were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel consumed not, them did Solomon make to pay tribute until this day. 9 But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no servants for his work; but they were men of war, and chief of his captains, and captains of his chariots and horsemen. 10 And these were the chief of king Solomon’s officers, even two hundred and fifty, that bare rule over the people.

8.6.1.en: As a king, a commander and a man of affairs, he did not seek his personal comfort, but employed many hands. He realized that it was in the people’s interest to encourage employment by every means, so that the state might not be afflicted with unemployment.

8.6.2.en: As for all the people that were left of the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which were not of Israel [7]

8.7.0.en: But of their children, who were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel consumed not, them did Solomon make to pay tribute until this day. [8]

8.7.1.en: There were many strangers in Israel who were left over from the Canaanites, and they were permitted to live among them, but not without work.

8.8.0.en: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no servants for his work; but they were men of war, and chief of his captains, and captains of his chariots and horsemen. [9]

8.9.0.en: And these were the chief of king Solomon’s officers, even two hundred and fifty, that bare rule over the people. [10]

8.10.s.en: 3. His care for his wife outside the city of David

8.10.0.en: And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David unto the house that he had built for her: for he said, My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of the LORD hath come. [11]

8.10.1.en: The bringing up of the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David to the house that Solomon built for her is, in the view of the Book of Kings (1 Kgs 9:24), a kind of distinction shown to her; but in the view of Chronicles, which is concerned with worship and holiness, it was not fitting for her to remain in the city of David, even if she had accepted the faith, because of the presence of her maidservants from Egypt, who might be idolaters.

8.10.2.en: It tells us of Solomon’s relationship with the daughter of Pharaoh. This carried a symbolic meaning. The Pharaoh kings were accustomed to give the daughters of their handmaids, who had no right to the throne, to the kings of the nations; but to Solomon Pharaoh gave his daughter as a lawful wife. She had the right to sit on the throne of Egypt if she had no son to inherit the throne. So this marriage is a sign confirming that Solomon had a lawful right in the land of Egypt. This conduct points to the submission of many kings and great men to the Lord Christ by their acceptance of faith in Him.

8.10.3.en: Solomon built a palace for the queen, the daughter of Pharaoh, and brought her up with her retinue outside the city of David. He wanted the city of David to remain holy, and he feared that the daughter of Pharaoh and her retinue might do things unbefitting the holiness of the city.

8.10.4.en: It is probable that the queen was an outsider, and perhaps some idols from Egypt were with her or with her retinue. Although, sadly, Solomon himself was afterward enticed by his idolatrous wives to build idolatrous altars.

8.10.5.en: Despite his good relations with the Gentiles, Solomon refused to let the daughter of Pharaoh dwell where the ark of the covenant was, even if she had accepted faith in God, for fear that there would be in the palace maidservants of hers from Egypt who were unbelievers.

8.11.s.en: 4. The ordering of the service of the temple

8.11.0.en: 12 Then Solomon offered burnt offerings unto the LORD on the altar of the LORD, which he had built before the porch, 13 Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. 14 And he appointed, according to the order of David his father, the courses of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their charges, to praise and minister before the priests, as the duty of every day required: the porters also by their courses at every gate: for so had David the man of God commanded. 15 And they departed not from the commandment of the king unto the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures. 16 Now all the work of Solomon was prepared unto the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD, and until it was finished. So the house of the LORD was perfected.

8.11.1.en: The religious and priestly services are mentioned in [12-16], especially the sacrifices of the burnt offering, which is not referred to in the Book of Kings.

8.11.2.en: The book does not refer to the details of the works that Solomon carried out, but is concerned to affirm that he arranged the daily, weekly, monthly and yearly service of the temple, especially the burnt offerings and the praise.

8.11.3.en: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings unto the LORD on the altar of the LORD, which he had built before the porch, [12]

8.12.0.en: Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles. [13]

8.12.1.en: Solomon’s role did not stop at building the temple and celebrating its dedication, but he continued to offer the holy sacrifices according to the Law of Moses [12-13].

8.12.2.en: Daily sacrifices were offered without ceasing, and weekly sacrifices on every Sabbath, which are double what is offered daily, and also additional monthly sacrifices at the new moons, and yearly sacrifices at the three great feasts.

8.12.3.en: Solomon’s heart, burning with longing for daily worship and for offering burnt offerings, incense and praises, was carrying this out according to the Law through the priests and Levites. In this period, before he turned aside after idolatrous women, he did not practice worship as a literal, routine work; rather, while keeping to good order according to the Law and the ordinance, he took part with his whole inner being, enjoying fellowship with God, offering prayers and enjoying heavenly thought through the shadows of the Old Testament.

8.12.4.en: He clung to God and loved Him, and felt with Jeremiah the prophet that the mercies of the Lord are new every morning (Lam 3:23). It is as though he repeated with him his saying: [The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him] (Lam 3:24).

8.12.5.en: v What are burnt offerings? The sacrifice burned entirely with fire; when the animal is placed on the altar and burned with fire, it is called a burnt offering.

8.12.6.en: May the divine fires lift us up wholly, and may we be kindled entirely...

8.12.7.en: Not only our souls are lifted up by this fire of wisdom, but our body also, as it receives immortality. Let it then be offered as a burnt offering, and death will be swallowed up!

8.12.8.en: St. Augustine v Both body and soul, that is, the whole man, desire to become a holy sacrifice to God. The psalmist declares that the soul is a sacrifice offered to God, saying: [A broken spirit is a sacrifice to God](*)[2].

8.12.9.en: v Let us offer our souls as a sacrifice through fasting. For we cannot offer to God anything better than this. The prophet confirms this by saying: [A broken spirit is a sacrifice to God, and a humble heart God will not despise](*). Offer, O man, yourself to God. Offer the offering of fasting. Do this to make yourself a pure sacrifice, a holy sacrifice, a living sacrifice that remains yours while you offer it to God[3].

8.12.10.en: Father Peter Chrysologus v He said to them: For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing I commanded them, saying, “And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath” (Jer 7:22-23; Zech 8:17)... He says: [The sacrifice to God is a broken spirit] (Ps 51:17); a broken heart is a fragrance to the Lord who formed it[4].

8.12.11.en: Epistle of Barnabas v This is the reason for which Job offers burnt offerings for his sons, lest they should have sinned unwittingly in thought[5].

8.12.12.en: St. Jerome v [I was afraid of all my works, knowing that You would not acquit me when I am guilty](**).

8.12.13.en: What works the blessed Job practiced, this holy history has made clear. For he had learned to appease his Creator by offering many burnt offerings. According to the number of his sons, as it is written, he rose up early in the morning and offered burnt offerings for each of them, cleansing them not only from unclean deeds but also from evil thoughts.

8.12.14.en: He recorded this for us by the testimony of the Holy Bible: “It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts” (Job 1:5).

8.12.16.en: v There is a necessity for this truth, that Christ the Savior of all should bear the Cross, for it was said of Him by the tongue of Isaiah: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder” (Isa 9:6). For the Cross is His government, by which He became King over the world. And since this was right, “He became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father” (Phil 2:8-10).

8.12.17.en: And also I think it must be observed here (that He should bear the Cross), because when the blessed Abraham went up the mountain that he saw to offer Isaac as a burnt offering at God’s command, he laid the wood upon the son, and this was a type of Christ bearing His Cross upon His shoulders, going up to the glory of His Cross. For the sufferings of Christ were His glories, as He Himself taught us: “Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him” (Jn 13:31)[6].

8.13.0.en: And he appointed, according to the order of David his father, the courses of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their charges (to praise and minister before the priests), as the duty of every day required: the porters also by their courses at every gate.

8.13.1.en: For so had David the man of God commanded. [14]

8.13.2.en: Solomon continued to offer sacrifices of praise, glorification and thanksgiving according to the commandment of his father David. He changed nothing of the order that his father David had set. And he did not stop, but worked “as the duty of every day required.”

8.13.3.en: The man of God: or the human being of God, a general expression in the Books of Kings, but one that rarely occurs in Chronicles; it is mentioned only of Moses (1 Chr 23:14), David, and another prophet (2 Chr 25:7, 9).

8.13.4.en: v It is fitting for the heart and mouth of the Christian never to cease from praising God, so that he does not glorify Him in joy and murmur against Him in hardship.

8.13.5.en: v He who prays with desire praises in his heart even if his tongue is silent. But if a man prays without longing, he is dumb before God even if his voice reaches the ears of men[7].

8.13.6.en: v Now, when we gather together in the church we praise God, but when each one goes to his work he seems to have ceased praising God. But may no one cease from an upright life, and so be a praiser of God continually. You cease to praise God when you turn aside from justice and from all that pleases God. But if you do not cease from an upright life, your life is eloquent, and the ear of God is opened to your heart[8].

8.13.7.en: v Whatever you do, do it well; by this you praise God[9].

8.13.8.en: v There we shall rest, and there we shall see. We shall see and love, we shall love and praise![10]

8.14.0.en: v How beautiful are those who sing the mysteries of God. Would that I too were joined to these songs in my prayer... Do not forbid a spiritual hymn, nor disdain to listen to it.

8.14.1.en: St. Methodius, Bishop of Olympus v Be like a soldier and make the night musical... Sing with the spirit and sing with the understanding also. Let your hymn be of the psalmist’s composing.

8.14.2.en: St. Jerome v The Kingdom of God is within you means the joy that the Holy Spirit plants in your hearts, being an icon and pledge of the eternal joy enjoyed by the souls of the saints[11].

8.15.0.en: And they departed not from the commandment of the king unto the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures. [15]

8.16.0.en: Now all the work of Solomon was prepared unto the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD, and until it was finished.

8.16.1.en: So the house of the LORD was perfected. [16]

8.17.s.en: 5. His commercial relations with foreign nations

8.17.0.en: 17 Then went Solomon to Eziongeber, and to Eloth, at the sea side in the land of Edom. 18 And Huram sent him by the hands of his servants ships, and servants that had knowledge of the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took thence four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and brought them to king Solomon.

8.17.1.en: Huram king of Tyre contributed not only to the building of the temple, but also to the prosperity of Solomon’s glorious kingdom.

8.17.2.en: Then went Solomon to Eziongeber, and to Eloth, at the sea side in the land of Edom. [17]

8.17.3.en: Eziongeber: on the Gulf of Aqaba beside Eloth.

8.18.0.en: And Huram sent him by the hands of his servants ships, and servants that had knowledge of the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took thence four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and brought them to king Solomon. [18]

8.18.2.en: As Solomon cared for international trade, he built a naval fleet, and had recourse to Huram king of Tyre to supply him with experts in maritime affairs to manage and operate the fleet.

8.18.3.en: He himself visited the ports of the two cities of Eloth and Eziongeber to examine the matter and to enter into international commercial relations.

8.18.4.en: Solomon benefited from the maritime experience of Huram king of Tyre, for his servants “had knowledge of the sea.”

8.18.5.en: The Jews had no people with experience in maritime work, since their experience was limited to the lakes within their own land. But Tyre, which lies on the sea, had experts in maritime work.

8.18.6.en: Let me offer You a daily sacrifice and unceasing praise!

8.18.7.en: v Solomon built a magnificent temple that drew the eyes of many.

8.18.8.en: Many thought that it would remain to the end of the ages.

8.18.9.en: And he set up great constructions of such magnitude.

8.18.10.en: And he built cities and fortresses!

8.18.11.en: What remains of all these constructions?!

8.18.12.en: Even the temple, which represented Your divine presence in the midst of Your people, was burned and demolished, and even its foundations vanished.

8.18.13.en: v Nothing remained but the pure hearts that followed the heart of David his father.

8.18.14.en: There remained the sacrifices of love, the burnt offerings of praise and the incense of pure prayers!

8.18.15.en: Grant me that my life may be transformed into a sacrifice of love.

8.18.16.en: Grant me that my whole being may become a spiritual harp, sending forth a unique symphony, in harmony with the praises of the heavenly ones!

8.18.17.en: v When shall I meet You on the clouds?!

8.18.18.en: And enjoy joining the chorus of the heavenly ones?!

8.18.19.en: When shall I sing the new song, and sing of Your love?!

8.18.20.en: In what language, I wonder, shall I sing in heaven, and speak with You, O Beloved?!

8.18.21.en: And what sacrifice shall I offer before Your holy throne?!
